sentence: Ayşe'nin yazdığı mektupları öğrenci dün okudu.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A less natural but structurally available analysis exploits the ambiguity of mektupları: it can be a possessed nominative noun rather than a plural accusative noun. On this analysis the possessed letter or letters will be the matrix subject, and öğrenci will be an indefinite object. Reading a student requires personification of the letters and a suitable interpretation of ‘read’; this is not the ordinary intended meaning. Ayşe'nin is nevertheless the overt subject of ‘write’, just as in the ordinary analysis. The silent relative operator is first placed in the relative verb's object position. Whole inflected words are retained, while silent I represents nonfinite agreement.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the relative clause for the possessed-subject alternative.

values.interpretation: the possessed letter or letters are what Ayşe wrote

values.morphology: plural noun with third-singular possession, or third-plural possession with possessed-number syncretism
values.reference: contextually supplied; not obligatorily identified with Ayşe

values.objectNP: abstract object Case without overt accusative marking

derivationStages.stageRecord: The relative operator moves to Spec-CP and leaves an object trace. The relative CP adjoins to the N′ headed by mektupları. A separate silent pronominal possessor occupies the nominal specifier: Ayşe'nin remains inside the relative clause and does not occupy this position. The noun is nominative and possessive, not accusative. Its whole-word form permits either a plural possessed noun with third-singular possession or third-plural possession with the number syncretism characteristic of -ları; these morphological alternatives do not change this constituent structure. No coreference between the silent possessor and Ayşe is imposed. The possessed NP is base-generated as the matrix subject. Öğrenci is a bare indefinite object, with abstract object Case but no overt accusative suffix. Dün adjoins to VP. Singular verbal agreement is compatible with a nonhuman plural subject in Turkish.
derivationStages.statement: Build a possessed matrix subject and an indefinite matrix object.

values.restriction: the bare indefinite object does not scramble

derivationStages.stageRecord: The final order places the indefinite object before dün. Bare unmarked objects in Turkish resist the ordinary scrambling available to accusative NPs, so öğrenci is not moved. Instead, the temporal adjunct is positioned by local rightward VP-adjunction, from its previously shown left-adjoined position. In this explicit GB implementation, the adjunct's movement leaves a silent adjunct trace, and the right-adjoined AdvP precedes the head-final verbal head because its landing domain is the object-containing projection below V⁰. This low positioning supplies the surface object–adverb–verb sequence without extracting the bare object or changing its Case licensing.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the possessed-subject reading with a low temporal-adjunct placement.
